label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. If a cookie banner offers no way to decline that works, accept it, report that as a problem, and carry on. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

findings.problem: The address search results and the Enter address manually option are plain list items. They cannot be reached with Tab, arrow keys, Enter or the elements list, so a keyboard user cannot pick an address or switch to manual entry. Continue to delivery stays disabled and the customer cannot get to payment.

The address search field has no accessible name. It is announced only as textbox, and the label Search for your address is separate text. The clear button is announced as Cross, and the search button is announced only as Search.
The Delivery section says the entered destination is outside the shipping zone before any address is entered. This is confusing and sounds like an error, and it was not announced as a change.

findings.problem: The country defaulted to United Kingdom although my region was set to [name], with no notice. A hint about numeric-only phone numbers appeared only after I had typed a phone number with brackets and a dash, and there was no error to tell me this.

A region and language dialog and a cookie dialog were both open on arrival. Focus started at the top of the page rather than inside them. Product names with an apostrophe were also hard to target. On the product page the Add to Basket button was first named Select a size, and nothing said the size was missing.
